title: Message, Part and Artifact
summary: A Message carries communication between client and agent, a Part is the typed content container inside messages and artifacts, and an Artifact is a deliverable produced by a task.
useIf: You design what a remote agent sends back and must decide what goes in a message, what goes in an artifact and which part type carries it.
avoidIf: You put task results in status messages: the spec says messages are not a reliable delivery mechanism.

explain.md: A `Message` has a `messageId`, a `role` (`ROLE_USER` or `ROLE_AGENT`), `parts`, and optional `taskId`, `contextId` and `referenceTaskIds`. A `Part` holds exactly one of `text`, `raw` (inline bytes, base64 in JSON), `url` (a reference) or `data` (any structured JSON value), plus `mediaType`, `filename` and `metadata`. An `Artifact` has an `artifactId`, optional `name` and `description`, and one or more parts [[r1]] [[tr2]].

The spec separates **communication from output**. Messages carry instructions, questions, clarifications and status. Results SHOULD be returned as artifacts of a task. Not every message is persisted in task history, and a client that reconnects to a stream may miss status messages, so messages must not carry critical information [[r1]]. Streamed artifacts can arrive in chunks: `append` extends an earlier artifact with the same id and `lastChunk` marks the end [[r1]].

explain.md: The card's `defaultInputModes` and `defaultOutputModes` list the media types an agent accepts and produces, and an unsupported part type returns `ContentTypeNotSupportedError`. Foundry's incoming A2A endpoint supports only the **text** modality (checked 2026-10-13) [[r17]].

whereToUse: Returning a generated report, image or dataset as a task artifact
Passing structured input such as a form or a parts list to a remote agent as a `data` part
Sending clarifying questions with `INPUT_REQUIRED` as a status message
Referencing large files by `url` so protocol payloads stay small
Declaring supported media types on the Agent Card so clients can negotiate

use: Put results in artifacts and keep messages for questions, scoping and progress
Use `data` parts with `application/json` when a program consumes the result
Use `url` parts for large or access-controlled files
avoid: Do not hide the only copy of a result in a status message
Do not inline large files as base64 in streamed events
Do not omit `mediaType`: receivers should not have to guess
flips: Peer is a Foundry agent: stay with text parts, since only text is supported there
Files are small and the network round trip matters more than payload size: inline `raw` can win over `url`
A downstream system needs strict schemas: define the `data` shape in the skill description and test it

pitfalls.symptom: A client reconnects and the result it was waiting for is gone
pitfalls.cause: The agent delivered the result only inside a status message, which can be missed after a disconnect
pitfalls.fix: Return deliverables as artifacts and fetch them with `GetTask` after reconnecting [[r1]]

pitfalls.symptom: Streaming slows and memory spikes on large outputs
pitfalls.cause: Large files were sent as inline `raw` parts in events
pitfalls.fix: Send a `url` part, or chunk artifacts with `append` and `lastChunk`

pitfalls.cause: A JSON string was placed in a `text` part without a media type
pitfalls.fix: Use a `data` part with `mediaType: application/json` and document the shape

scenarios.title: A 40 MB report from a long-running job
scenarios.situation: A remote agent produces a 40 MB PDF after a 15-minute job. Callers sometimes disconnect before it finishes. The file is confidential.
unknowns: How long can the agent keep the file?
Can links be authenticated and expiring?
scenarios.question: How does the agent deliver the report?

options.name: A task artifact with a `url` part pointing to an authenticated, expiring link
options.why: The result survives disconnects, stays out of the event stream and access can be controlled.
options.tradeoff: The agent must run file storage and issue links.

options.name: A task artifact with an inline `raw` part
options.why: A single self-contained response with no extra fetch.
options.tradeoff: A 40 MB file becomes about 53 MB of base64 in JSON.

options.name: Stream the bytes in status messages
options.why: Status messages may be missed on reconnect and are not for deliverables.
options.tradeoff: Right only for transient progress text.

flips.if: Callers cannot fetch URLs from the agent's domain
flips.then: Chunk it as an artifact over the stream with `append` and `lastChunk`.

scenarios.takeaway: Deliverables are artifacts, and big ones travel by reference.

scenarios.title: A structured quote consumed by code
scenarios.situation: An order-processing agent calls a supplier agent for quotes and parses the price, currency and lead time programmatically. Quotes must be reproducible in audits.
unknowns: Does the supplier version its output schema?
Is a human summary also needed?
scenarios.question: How should the supplier return the quote?

options.name: An artifact with a `data` part (`application/json`) and an optional text part for humans
options.why: Typed fields for code, a retained artifact for audits and a readable summary alongside.
options.tradeoff: Both sides must agree on and version the JSON shape.

options.name: JSON inside a `text` part
options.why: Works with text-only peers and needs no extra modality.
options.tradeoff: Parsing is fragile and the media type does not say it is JSON.

options.name: A status message sentence the caller parses with an LLM
options.why: Non-deterministic parsing of a message that may not be persisted.
options.tradeoff: Fine for a human chat summary, not for money.

flips.if: The peer is Foundry and supports only text
flips.then: Use JSON in a text part with a documented shape.

flips.if: Only a human reads the quote

quiz.q: Where should an agent return the deliverable of a task?
options: In a status message on the task
As an artifact of the task
In the `metadata` of the next request
quiz.explain: The spec says results SHOULD be artifacts and messages are for communication. Status messages may not be persisted or replayed, the card describes the agent and request metadata is not a result channel.

quiz.q: A `Part` holds exactly one of which content fields? Select all that apply.
quiz.explain: The content fields are `text`, `raw`, `url` and `data`. `artifactId` identifies an artifact and is not a part field.

flashcards.front: What is the difference between a Message and an Artifact in A2A?
flashcards.back: Messages carry communication: questions, scoping and status. Artifacts carry task deliverables. Results SHOULD be artifacts.

flashcards.front: Which four content fields can a Part use?
flashcards.back: Exactly one of `text`, `raw`, `url` or `data`, plus `mediaType`, `filename` and `metadata`.

flashcards.front: What do `append` and `lastChunk` do on an artifact update?
flashcards.back: `append` extends an earlier artifact with the same id. `lastChunk` marks the final chunk, so large artifacts can stream.
